purpose: RYDAPT is used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including a type of leukemia called acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that has a specific gene change called FLT3 mutation. It is also used for rare conditions called systemic mastocytosis, where too many abnormal mast cells build up in the body. Your doctor will use special tests to determine if this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: RYDAPT works by blocking certain proteins called kinases that cancer cells need to grow and survive. Think of these proteins as 'on switches' for cancer cell growth — RYDAPT helps turn those switches off. By doing this, it slows down or stops the cancer cells from multiplying.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and stomach upset are very common, especially in the beginning. You may also experience headache, muscle or joint pain, feeling tired or weak, low blood cell counts, mouth sores, and upper respiratory infections. Swelling in your hands or feet may also occur.
warnings: RYDAPT can cause a serious lung problem called pulmonary toxicity — call your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, a new cough, or fever. It can also lower your blood cell counts, making you more prone to infections, bleeding, or anemia. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should not use this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood to unsafe levels.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg (two 25 mg capsules) taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart. Always take it with food to help reduce nausea. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. Take it at the same times each day and follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
